main_body: Thatched hut: a tall tiered thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank front wall with a door and a window (rows 37-63)
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope, rows 0-35, lighter bands with darker tier shadows. A bright eave lip sits at rows 34-36.
evidence: Down the middle column, the roof slope is a large light thatch surface with stepped tiers, the same way the reference tile roofs read. A bright eave line at rows 34-36 is followed by a dark shadow band at rows 37-39. The plank wall below has an inset door with a dark frame and iron straps, and a recessed window with a dark interior. The roof is a real slope, not a hat line, and no receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 5 tones with per-tier highlights and darker gaps. The walls have plank grain in several browns. The outline is a dark brown that follows the material rather than a black sticker line. The door has straps, a handle and a stone step, and the window has a shutter and a sill. There are no big flat fills. Detail density is comparable to the reference houses, though the roof is a little more repetitive.
